arxiv-2102-08616.title: Conserving Lattice Gauge Theory for Finite Systems
arxiv-2102-08616.creator: ARAlexander Rothkopf
arxiv-2102-08616.description: Abstract In this study I develop a novel action for lattice gauge theory for finite systems, which accommodates non-periodic boundary conditions, implements the proper integral form of Gauss’ law and exhibits an inherently symmetric energy momentum tensor, all while realizing automatic 𝒪 ⁡ ( a ) {\cal O}(a) improvement.

arxiv-2203-05356.title: An addendum to “Mild solutions to semilinear stochastic partial differential equations with locally monotone coefficients” Thanks: I am grateful to Michael Röckner for fruitful discussions. I am also grateful to the referee for helpful comments. Moreover, I gratefully acknowledge financial support f
arxiv-2203-05356.creator: Stefan Tappe
arxiv-2203-05356.description: Abstract . In this addendum we provide an existence and uniqueness result for mild solutions to semilinear stochastic partial differential equations driven by Wiener processes and Poisson random measures in the framework of the semigroup approach with locally monotone coefficients, where the semigroup is allowed to be pseudo-contractive.

arxiv-2312-03021.title: Effective generation of Hecke algebras and explicit estimates of Sato–Tate type
arxiv-2312-03021.creator: Ben Moore
arxiv-2312-03021.description: Abstract . Assuming the Riemann hypothesis for L L -functions attached to primitive Dirichlet characters, modular cusp forms, and their tensor products and symmetric squares, we write down explicit finite sets of Hecke operators that span the Hecke algebras acting on the spaces of modular forms of weight greater than two with squarefree level. 1.

arxiv-2401-13966.title: The Avoidance Principle for Noncompact Hypersurfaces Moving by Mean Curvature Flow
arxiv-2401-13966.creator: Brian White
arxiv-2401-13966.description: Abstract . Consider a pair of smooth, possibly noncompact, properly immersed hypersurfaces moving by mean curvature flow, or, more generally, a pair of weak set flows. We prove that if the ambient space is Euclidean space and if the distance between the two surfaces is initially nonzero, then the surfaces remain disjoint at all subsequent times.

arxiv-2412-02524.title: General Theory for Group Resetting with Application to Avoidance
arxiv-2412-02524.creator: Juhee Lee, Seong-Gyu Yang, Hye Jin Park, Ludvig Lizana
arxiv-2412-02524.description: Abstract We present a general theoretical framework for group resetting dynamics in multi-particle systems in a drift potential. While traditional resetting models typically focus on a single particle, our setup considers a group of particles whose collective dynamics determine the resetting process.

arxiv-2501-00277.title: Efficient Human-in-the-Loop Active Learning: A Novel Framework for Data Labeling in AI Systems Thanks: Corresponding author
arxiv-2501-00277.creator: Yiran Huang, Jian-Feng Yang
arxiv-2501-00277.description: Abstract Modern AI systems rely heavily on labeled data, yet labeling is often expensive and labor-intensive, especially when requiring special skills such as reading radiology images by physicians. To most efficiently use experts’ time for data labeling, one promising approach is human-in-the-loop active learning.

arxiv-2509-12982.title: Out of Distribution Detection in Self-adaptive Robots with AI-powered Digital Twins
arxiv-2509-12982.creator: Erblin Isaku, Hassan Sartaj, Shaukat Ali, Beatriz Sanguino, Tongtong Wang, Guoyuan Li, Houxiang Zhang, and Thomas Peyrucain
arxiv-2509-12982.description: Abstract Self-adaptive robots (SARs) in complex, uncertain environments must proactively detect and address abnormal behaviors, including out-of-distribution (OOD) cases. To this end, digital twins offer a valuable solution for OOD detection. Thus, we present a digital twin-based approach for OOD detection ( ODiSAR ) in SARs.

arxiv-2601-04814.title: The Rezk Completion for Elementary Topoi
arxiv-2601-04814.creator: Kobe Wullaert, Niels van der Weide
arxiv-2601-04814.description: Abstract The development of category theory in univalent foundations and the formalization thereof is an active field of research. Categories in that setting are often assumed to be univalent which means that identities and isomorphisms of objects coincide. One consequence hereof is that equivalences and identities coincide for univalent categories and that structure on univalent categories transfers along equivalences.

arxiv-2604-07832.title: The Schwarz function and the shrinking of the Szegő curve: electrostatic, hydrodynamic, and random matrix models
arxiv-2604-07832.creator: Gabriel Álvarez, Luis Martínez Alonso, Elena Medina

pmc-10622424.title: Characterization of net-zero pozzolanic potential of thermally-derived metakaolin samples for sustainable carbon neutrality construction
pmc-10622424.creator: K C Onyelowe, A Naghizadeh, F I Aneke, D-P N Kontoni, M E Onyia, M Welman-Purchase, A M Ebid, E I Adah, Liberty U Stephen
pmc-10622424.description: Metakaolin (MK) is one of the most sustainable cementitious construction materials, which is derived through a direct heating procedure known as calcination. Calcination process takes place substantially lower temperatures than that required for Portland cement, making it a more environmentally sustainable alternative to traditional cement.

pmc-11526525.title: Prenatal exposure to air pollution during the early and middle stages of pregnancy is associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes at ages 1 to 3 years
pmc-11526525.creator: Frederica Perera, Yuqi Miao, Zev Ross, Virginia Rauh, Amy Margolis, Lori Hoepner, Kylie W Riley, Julie Herbstman, Shuang Wang
pmc-11526525.description: BackgroundA large body of data shows that fetal brain development is vulnerable to disruption by air pollution experienced by the mother during pregnancy, adversely affecting cognitive and psychomotor capabilities during childhood (De Asis-Cruz et al., Biol Psychiatry 7:480–90, 2022; Morgan ZEM et al., Environ Health 22:11, 2023).

pmc-12503246.title: Viral interferon antagonism shapes host tropism
pmc-12503246.creator: Felix Streicher, Amandine Chantharath, Nolwenn Jouvenet
pmc-12503246.description: Outbreaks of zoonotic viruses in human populations highlight the need to understand the molecular factors that influence viral host tropism and interspecies transmission. A virus’s host range is determined not only by the expression of host factors that facilitate viral entry and replication, but also by the virus’s ability to evade host antiviral immunity.

pmc-12737618.title: Detection of Bovine Viral Diarrhoea Virus in a Case Series of Clinically Cachectic Cattle from Tiaret, Algeria
pmc-12737618.creator: Nacira Ghenoumat, Houari Hemida, Assia Boumezrag, Dimitrije Glišić, Sofija Šolaja, Ljubiša Veljović, Vesna Milićević, Librado Carrasco Otero, Wentao Li
pmc-12737618.description: Simple SummaryBovine viral diarrhoea (BVD) is an important infectious disease of cattle that causes health and economic problems. This report describes the detection and genetic identification of BVDV-1f in a clinical series of cachectic cattle from Tiaret province, Algeria. One hundred clinically cachectic cattle from ten herds were sampled opportunistically and tested using serological and molecular methods.

pmc-13145483.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A898 TIME TO IMAGING AND REPERFUSION STATUS MODIFY CT PERFUSION PREDICTION OF MALIGNANT CEREBRAL INFARCTION
pmc-13145483.creator: Antonio Doncel-Moriano, Alejandro Rodríguez Vázquez, Andrea Cabero-Arnold, Irene Rosa Batlle, Arturo Renú, Inés Bartolomé, Salvatore Rudilosso, Martha Vargas, Xabier Urra, Angel Chamorro
pmc-13145483.description: Background and aimsMalignant cerebral infarction (MCI) is a life-threatening complication of large vessel occlusion (LVO). Baseline CT-perfusion (CTP) thresholds and ASPECTS predict MCI, but their performance may depend on time-to-imaging and reperfusion success. We evaluated whether these factors influence the predictive accuracy of baseline markers (ASPECTS, relative cerebral blood volume [rCBV], relative cerebral blood flow [rCBF]) for MCI.

pmc-13300158.title: Synergistic Induction of Caspase-8-Mediated Leukaemic Cell Death by Fisetin and Pinocembrin
pmc-13300158.creator: Narawan Kaewthawee, Ankita Sharma, James Michael Brimson, Sirikalaya Brimson

pmc-13392359.title: Deep learning-based tooth axis estimation from 3D tooth crowns using quaternion representation and multi-loss optimization
pmc-13392359.creator: Geunhye Kim, Sena Lee, Junghun Han, Eun-Hack Andrew Choi, Yongkyu Jin, Chooryung Judi Chung, Sejung Yang
pmc-13392359.description: Tooth axis estimation plays a key role in various digital dental workflows, including orthodontic diagnosis and prosthetic design. In clinical practice, tooth axes are typically determined by jointly considering crown morphology and radiographic information; however, this process is subjective and time-consuming.

pmc-13540174.title: Outer membrane vesicles from Fusobacterium necrophorum elicit protective immunity in mice and robust immune responses in sheep
pmc-13540174.creator: Pengyu Zhao, Jiancheng Jiang, Ning Yang, Rongqi Liu, Kai Jiang, Lan Bi, Xianjing He, Donghua Guo
pmc-13540174.description: Fusobacterium necrophorum is a major opportunistic pathogen of ruminants that causes foot rot and liver abscesses and contributes to substantial economic losses. Current vaccines provide limited protection. Here, we prepared and evaluated outer membrane vesicles (OMVs)-based vaccine candidate derived from F. necrophorum. OMVs were purified by density-gradient centrifugation and were characterized for morphology, composition, and immunological activity.

pmc-13548000.title: Molecular Tumor Boards in Malignant Melanoma: Uncovering Challenges and Opportunities in a Bicenter Retrospective Analysis in Germany
pmc-13548000.creator: Glenn Geidel, Theresa Lowinus, Patrick Metzger, Rebecca Czurda, Vincent Schipperges, Ulrike Paul, Alessandra Rünger, Julian Kött, Isabel Heidrich, Saskia Lehr, Julia Kühn, Heiko Becker, Cornelius Miething, Martin Werner, Silke Laßmann, Justus Duyster, Tilman Brummer, Ronald Simon, Winfried Alsdorf,
pmc-13548000.description: Despite therapeutic advancements, approximately 50% of advanced melanoma patients succumb to metastatic disease. Molecular tumor boards (MTB) aim to identify targetable molecular alterations to guide individualized treatment strategies. Yet, real‐world data on patient selection, referral timing, recommendation rates, implementation, and clinical impact remain limited.

pmc-13678082.title: Microalgal Synthetic Biotechnology: From Genetic Models to Deployable Photosynthetic Chassis
pmc-13678082.creator: Jin Liu
pmc-13678082.description: Microalgae have long been considered promising platforms for producing biochemicals and supporting environmental applications. Realizing this potential will require turning microalgal species into predictable and reusable engineering platforms. However, it remains challenging to engineer such evolutionarily diverse, compartmentalized photosynthetic eukaryotes in a predictable way, because their behavior depends strongly on organelle organization, gene-expression context, and cultivation conditions.

pmc-13679214.title: When pupillometry indices disagree: does QPi add prognostic information beyond NPi?
pmc-13679214.creator: Li-Xia Xu
pmc-13679214.description: exposure. These findings support the authors’ conclusion that the two indices should not be considered interchangeable. However, an important clinical question remains: when NPi and QPi disagree, does QPi provide additional prognostic information, or does the disagreement primarily reflect differences in measurement susceptibility? The distinction matters because association with outcome and incremental clinical information are not equivalent.

uslaw-usc-t33-s4265.title: 33 U.S.C. § 4265 — Consideration of marine debris in negotiating international agreements
uslaw-usc-t33-s4265.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t33-s4265.description: United States Code, Title 33 (Navigation And Navigable Waters); Chapter 55 (Save Our Seas 2.0); Subchapter II (Enhanced Global Engagement To Combat Marine Debris). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In negotiating any relevant international agreement with any country or countries after December 18, 2020, the President shall, as appropriate— (1) consider the impact of land-based sources of plastic waste and other solid.
